text: This lab walks through a full, realistic reproduction attempt end to end — screening, extraction, running, and diagnosing a discrepancy — using this chapter's full toolkit on one worked scenario.

This lesson covers carrying a reproduction attempt through every stage covered in this chapter without skipping one, computing and interpreting a relative difference between your result and a paper's reported result, deciding whether a discrepancy needs further diagnosis or is within reasonable bounds, and writing a short, honest reproduction report — the actual deliverable format you'll use again in your capstone.

The scenario: you've selected a recent, modest paper benchmarking a specific error-mitigation technique on a three-qubit circuit, with the circuit and parameters specified in the text. The paper reports that mitigation reduces measured error by 0.18, from a baseline error rate to a mitigated error rate. Your task is to extract the methodology, run your own version, and judge the result.

With a hypothetical result of your own — baseline error 0.24, mitigated error 0.085 — your measured error reduction is 0.24 minus 0.085, which is 0.155. The relative difference from the paper's reported 0.18 is about negative 13.9 percent, checked by direct calculation. Whether that 14 percent gap is a real discrepancy depends entirely on the paper's stated uncertainty — and if the paper reports essentially none, you have no principled way to judge whether 14 percent is close, which is itself worth stating plainly rather than guessing.

The diagnostic priority, per the previous lesson's checklist: re-check your own circuit and mitigation implementation against your methodology document first, re-confirm every parameter especially the mitigation sub-technique, revisit any detail you had to guess at during extraction, and only then consider hardware differences or an actual disagreement with the paper. A good write-up states the measured numbers precisely, names the specific missing information that prevents a confident conclusion, and states a concrete next step — it doesn't claim success or failure outright.
